################################################################################
## SUPPLEMENTARY GAP TRANSCRIPT
## Krohn-Rhodes / holonomy structure of canonical DN and WTA neural motifs
##
## Software:  GAP 4.15.1;  packages: sgpdec 1.2.0, semigroups 5.6.3,
##            digraphs 1.15.0, orb 5.1.0, images 1.4.0, datastructures 0.4.3
##
## Reproduce with:
##     gap -q -A -o 8g transcript.g
## after placing gap_systems.g (generated by export_gap.py) in the same
## directory.  gap_systems.g defines, for each system NAME, the variables
## deg_NAME, gens_NAME and gennames_NAME, plus the list SYSTEMS.
##
## CONVENTIONS
##   GAP is ONE-BASED: GAP point p corresponds to paper state p-1.
##   A transformation on X={0..n-1} is written as the tuple (f(0),...,f(n-1))
##   in the paper and as its one-based image list in GAP.
##   DN 4-state:  X_D = {0,1,2,3}.
##   WTA:         X_W = {0,1}^3 encoded q = 4*b1 + 2*b2 + g.
##   Composite:   32 states, idx(d,w) = 8*d + w.
##
## A note on what a HOLONOMY GROUP acts on, which matters for how these
## numbers may be quoted.  For an image set C of the skeleton:
##   * PermutatorGroup(sk, C) is the group of permutations of the RAW STATES
##     of C induced by words that map C onto itself.
##   * The holonomy group is the image of that group acting on the TILES of
##     C (the maximal proper subsets of C that are themselves image sets).
##   These differ in general.  When every tile is a singleton the two
##   coincide and the group genuinely permutes states; when the tiles are
##   larger, the group permutes SUBSETS and no claim about individual states
##   is licensed.  Both are reported below.
################################################################################

gap> LoadPackage("sgpdec", false);;
gap> SgpDecOptionsRec.SMALL_GROUPS := true;;
gap> Read("gap_systems.g");

################################################################################
## SYSTEM DN3   (degree 3)
################################################################################
gap> gens_DN3;
[ Transformation( [ 1, 1, 1 ] ), Transformation( [ 3, 2, 1 ] ), Transformation( [ 3, 3, 2 ] ) ]
##   generator names: D0, D1, D2

## ---- transition monoid ----
gap> M := Monoid(gens_DN3);; Size(M);
13
##   (Semigroup(gens) omits the identity unless it is a product of
##    generators; Size(Semigroup(gens)) = 13 here, so the paper's |M| is the Monoid value.)
gap> IsAperiodicSemigroup(M);
false
gap> Length(Idempotents(M));
6
gap> Number(AsList(M), t -> t^3 <> t^4);   ## non-aperiodic elements
3
gap> Size(GroupOfUnits(M));
2
gap> StructureDescription(Range(IsomorphismPermGroup(GroupOfUnits(M))));
C2

## ---- aperiodicity of each generator ----
##   t is aperiodic iff t^n = t^(n+1) (n = degree): every cycle of the
##   functional graph is a fixed point.
gap> t := gens_DN3[1);; t^3 = t^4;   ## D0
true
gap> t := gens_DN3[2);; t^3 = t^4;   ## D1
false
gap> t := gens_DN3[3);; t^3 = t^4;   ## D2
false

## ---- holonomy skeleton ----
gap> sk := Skeleton(M);; DepthOfSkeleton(sk);
3
gap> DisplayHolonomyComponents(sk);
1: (2,C2)
2: (2,C2)
##   Reading: "level: n" is a trivial component on n tiles;
##   "(n,G)" is a component of n tiles carrying group G.

## ---- group components, with supports decoded ----
gap> gc := GroupComponents(sk);; rs := RepresentativeSets(sk);;
##   level 1 slot 1: Group( [ (1,2) ] )  |G| = 2  C2
##       representative set : {0 1 2}
##       tiles permuted     : {0 1} | {1 2}
##   level 2 slot 1: Group( [ (1,2) ] )  |G| = 2  C2
##       representative set : {1 2}
##       tiles permuted     : {1} | {2}

## ---- faithfulness of the holonomy decomposition ----
gap> hcs := HolonomyCascadeSemigroup(M);;
gap> hom := HomomorphismTransformationSemigroup(hcs);;
gap> Size(Range(hom));
13
gap> AsSortedList(M) = AsSortedList(Range(hom));
true
gap> ForAll(AsList(M), t -> AsHolonomyTransformation(AsHolonomyCascade(t, sk), sk) = t);
true
##   TRUE means every element of M is recovered exactly from its
##   cascade coordinates: the decomposition is faithful.

################################################################################
## SYSTEM DN4   (degree 4)
################################################################################
gap> gens_DN4;
[ Transformation( [ 1, 1, 1, 1 ] ), Transformation( [ 2, 2, 1, 1 ] ), Transformation( [ 3, 2, 2, 2 ] ), Transformation( [ 4, 3, 3, 2 ] ) ]
##   generator names: D0, D1, D2, D3

## ---- transition monoid ----
gap> M := Monoid(gens_DN4);; Size(M);
24
##   (Semigroup(gens) omits the identity unless it is a product of
##    generators; Size(Semigroup(gens)) = 23 here, so the paper's |M| is the Monoid value.)
gap> IsAperiodicSemigroup(M);
false
gap> Length(Idempotents(M));
8
gap> Number(AsList(M), t -> t^4 <> t^5);   ## non-aperiodic elements
3
gap> Size(GroupOfUnits(M));
1
gap> StructureDescription(Range(IsomorphismPermGroup(GroupOfUnits(M))));
1

## ---- aperiodicity of each generator ----
##   t is aperiodic iff t^n = t^(n+1) (n = degree): every cycle of the
##   functional graph is a fixed point.
gap> t := gens_DN4[1);; t^4 = t^5;   ## D0
true
gap> t := gens_DN4[2);; t^4 = t^5;   ## D1
true
gap> t := gens_DN4[3);; t^4 = t^5;   ## D2
true
gap> t := gens_DN4[4);; t^4 = t^5;   ## D3
true

## ---- holonomy skeleton ----
gap> sk := Skeleton(M);; DepthOfSkeleton(sk);
4
gap> DisplayHolonomyComponents(sk);
1: 2
2: 2
3: (2,C2)
##   Reading: "level: n" is a trivial component on n tiles;
##   "(n,G)" is a component of n tiles carrying group G.

## ---- group components, with supports decoded ----
gap> gc := GroupComponents(sk);; rs := RepresentativeSets(sk);;
##   level 3 slot 1: Group( [ (1,2) ] )  |G| = 2  C2
##       representative set : {0 1}
##       tiles permuted     : {0} | {1}

## ---- faithfulness of the holonomy decomposition ----
gap> hcs := HolonomyCascadeSemigroup(M);;
gap> hom := HomomorphismTransformationSemigroup(hcs);;
gap> Size(Range(hom));
23
gap> AsSortedList(M) = AsSortedList(Range(hom));
false
##   The set difference is exactly:
##   [ IdentityTransformation ]
##   i.e. only the identity, because Range(hom) is built with
##   Semigroup(...) from the cascade generators.  This is a
##   Semigroup-vs-Monoid bookkeeping artefact, NOT a failure of the
##   decomposition.  The elementwise test below is the real check.
gap> ForAll(AsList(M), t -> AsHolonomyTransformation(AsHolonomyCascade(t, sk), sk) = t);
true
##   TRUE means every element of M is recovered exactly from its
##   cascade coordinates: the decomposition is faithful.

##   NOT ATTEMPTED for this system.  The holonomy cascade has
##   coordinate-value counts [ 18, 6, 6, 5, 4, 8, 7, 8, 6, 2, 4 ],
##   i.e. a cascade state space of 278691840 tuples;
##   constructing a single cascade element exhausts memory at -o 14g.
##   The skeleton, its depth, and all group components above are exact;
##   only the explicit cascade reconstruction is omitted.

##       tiles permuted     : {4=(D:0,W:4) 12=(D:1,W:4)} | {4=(D:0,W:4) 17=(D:2,W:1)} | {12=(D:1,W:4) 17=(D:2,W:1)}

##   level 17 slot 1: Group( [ (1,2) ] )  |G| = 2  C2

## ---- faithfulness of the holonomy decomposition ----
##   NOT ATTEMPTED for this system.  The holonomy cascade has
##   coordinate-value counts [ 16, 26, 34, 12, 12, 19, 20, 21, 21, 15, 12, 21, 3, 9, 24, 6, 2, 12, 4, 2, 6 ],
##   i.e. a cascade state space of 5778664237486728806400 tuples;

false

##   [ IdentityTransformation ]
##   i.e. only the identity, because Range(hom) is built with
##   Semigroup(...) from the cascade generators.  This is a
##   Semigroup-vs-Monoid bookkeeping artefact, NOT a failure of the
##   decomposition.  The elementwise test below is the real check.
gap> ForAll(AsList(M), t -> AsHolonomyTransformation(AsHolonomyCascade(t, sk), sk) = t);
true
##   TRUE means every element of M is recovered exactly from its
##   cascade coordinates: the decomposition is faithful.

################################################################################
## TARGETED CHECKS OF THE CLAIMS MADE IN THE TEXT
################################################################################
## For a state subset C we report:
##   PermutatorGroup(sk, C)  -- action on the RAW STATES of C
##   holonomy group          -- induced action on the TILES of C
##   the subduction class of C and that class's transversal representative
##     (holonomy groups are conjugate, hence isomorphic, along a class, so a
##      set that is not the chosen representative still carries the group of
##      its class -- it simply does not appear in GroupComponents output)

## (b) DN4: does the level-3 C2 correspond to the audit witness cycle 2<->1?
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 2, 3 ], 4);;   ## paper states [ 1, 2 ] = {1 2}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
3
gap> PermutatorGroup(sk, C);
Group( [ (2,3) ] )
##   C2 on the raw states
gap> Image(PermutatorHolonomyHomomorphism(sk, C));
Group( [ (1,2) ] )
##   C2 on the 2 tiles: {1} | {2}
##   All tiles are SINGLETONS, so this group permutes individual states.
gap> Length(SubductionClassOfSet(sk, C));
3
##   class representative = level 3 slot 1 = {0 1}

##     DN4: the transversal representative of that same class.
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 1, 2 ], 4);;   ## paper states [ 0, 1 ] = {0 1}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
3
gap> PermutatorGroup(sk, C);
Group( [ (1,2) ] )
##   C2 on the raw states
gap> Image(PermutatorHolonomyHomomorphism(sk, C));
Group( [ (1,2) ] )
##   C2 on the 2 tiles: {0} | {1}
##   All tiles are SINGLETONS, so this group permutes individual states.
gap> Length(SubductionClassOfSet(sk, C));
3
##   class representative = level 3 slot 1 = {0 1}

## (a) WTA: is there a C2 supported on {4,5} (GAP {5,6})?
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 5, 6 ], 8);;   ## paper states [ 4, 5 ] = {4=(1,0,0) 5=(1,0,1)}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
5
gap> PermutatorGroup(sk, C);
Group( [ (5,6) ] )
##   C2 on the raw states
gap> Image(PermutatorHolonomyHomomorphism(sk, C));
Group( [ (1,2) ] )
##   C2 on the 2 tiles: {4=(1,0,0)} | {5=(1,0,1)}
##   All tiles are SINGLETONS, so this group permutes individual states.
gap> Length(SubductionClassOfSet(sk, C));
15
##   class representative = level 5 slot 1 = {4=(1,0,0) 5=(1,0,1)}

## (a) WTA: and on the symmetric counterpart {2,3} (GAP {3,4})?
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 3, 4 ], 8);;   ## paper states [ 2, 3 ] = {2=(0,1,0) 3=(0,1,1)}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
5
gap> PermutatorGroup(sk, C);
Group( [ (3,4) ] )
##   C2 on the raw states
gap> Image(PermutatorHolonomyHomomorphism(sk, C));
Group( [ (1,2) ] )
##   C2 on the 2 tiles: {2=(0,1,0)} | {3=(0,1,1)}
##   All tiles are SINGLETONS, so this group permutes individual states.
gap> Length(SubductionClassOfSet(sk, C));
15
##   class representative = level 5 slot 1 = {4=(1,0,0) 5=(1,0,1)}

## (c) W_to_D KEY CLAIM: a nontrivial group whose support contains BOTH composite state 4 = (D:0,W:4) and 13 = (D:1,W:5) (GAP points 5 and 14).
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 5, 14 ], 32);;   ## paper states [ 4, 13 ] = {4=(D:0,W:4) 13=(D:1,W:5)}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
17

gap> Length(SubductionClassOfSet(sk, C));
45
##   class representative = level 17 slot 1 = {10=(D:1,W:2) 19=(D:2,W:3)}

## (d) prod: the corresponding pair 12,13 in the product control.
gap> C := FiniteSet([ 13, 14 ], 32);;   ## paper states [ 12, 13 ] = {12=(D:1,W:4) 13=(D:1,W:5)}
gap> DepthOfSet(sk, C);
7

Group( [ (13,14) ] )
##   C2 on the raw states

##   class representative = level 10 slot 1 = {12=(D:1,W:4) 13=(D:1,W:5)}

################################################################################
## IS THE GROUP ACTION INHERITED FROM A FACTOR, OR GENUINELY COMPOSITE?
################################################################################
## A permutation of composite states idx = 8*d + w is INHERITED from the WTA
## factor if it never changes d, and from the DN factor if it never changes
## w.  It is COMPOSITE only if some state is moved to a state differing in
## BOTH coordinates -- such a permutation is not a permutation of either
## factor alone.  Counts below are over all image sets of each skeleton
## carrying a nontrivial permutator group (see compositeness.g).
##
## An explicit witness for the W_to_D key claim:
gap> sw := Filtered(AsList(M), t -> OnFiniteSet(C,t)=C and 5^t=14 and 14^t=5);;
gap> Length(sw);
13
gap> sw[1];
Transformation( [ 13, 13, 10, 5, 14, 5, 5, 5, 13, 13, 18, 5, 22, 5, 5, 5, 13, 13, 18, 5, 22, 5, 5, 5, 13, 13, 18, 13, 22, 13, 13, 13 ] )
##   This element maps paper state 4 = (D:0,W:4) -> 13 = (D:1,W:5)
##                   and paper state 13 = (D:1,W:5) -> 4 = (D:0,W:4)
##   Both the DN and the WTA coordinate change, so the swap is composite:
##   it is not induced by a permutation of either factor on its own.

## Counts over all image sets carrying a nontrivial permutator group
## (produced by compositeness.g; full per-window detail in
##  holonomy_compositeness.csv):
##
##   system    windows   W-only(inherited)  D-only   COMPOSITE
##   prod         34             27         7          0
##   D_to_W       46             31         0         15
##   W_to_D       57             12        10         35
##
##   prod has ZERO composite windows: every group action in the product
##   system is inherited from one factor.  Both cascades have composite
##   windows.  This is the control-vs-cascade contrast of the paper.
##   D_to_W composite-window group types: {'C4': 3, 'C2': 12}
##   W_to_D composite-window group types: {'C2': 35}

################################################################################
## FAITHFULNESS: SUMMARY OF WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT VERIFIED
################################################################################
## Elementwise round-trip
##   AsHolonomyTransformation(AsHolonomyCascade(t, sk), sk) = t
## verified for EVERY element of M:
##   DN3 (13), DN4 (24), WTA (326), prod (576), rec_sync (9),
##   rec_async_D (8), rec_async_W (8).
##
## Setwise test  AsSortedList(M) = AsSortedList(Range(hom))  on those same
## seven systems:
##
##   system        Size(Range(hom))   |M|    setwise
##   DN3                        13     13    true
##   DN4                        23     24    false
##   WTA                       325    326    false
##   prod                      575    576    false
##   rec_sync                    8      9    false
##   rec_async_D                 7      8    false
##   rec_async_W                 7      8    false
##
## Where it is false the set difference is exactly [IdentityTransformation],
## because Range(hom) is built with Semigroup(...) from the cascade
## generators and so omits the identity unless the identity is itself a
## product of generators.  DN3 is precisely that exception: there the
## identity IS a generator product, Size(Semigroup(gens_DN3)) = 13 = |M|,
## and the setwise test passes.  The elementwise test above is the one to
## quote, since its outcome does not depend on this accident.
##
## No setwise result exists for D_to_W or W_to_D -- the cascade was not
## constructed for them (see below), so for those two the test is UNPROVEN,
## not false.
##
## D_to_W (|M| = 3149, depth 12): the exhaustive sweep exhausted memory.
##   A bounded probe -- all 4 generators, the identity, and 120 further
##   elements sampled across the monoid, 125 distinct elements in total --
##   returned 125 successes and 0 mismatches.
##
## W_to_D (|M| = 3084, depth 22): NOT ATTEMPTED.  The holonomy cascade for
##   this skeleton has coordinate-value counts
##     [16,26,34,12,12,19,20,21,21,15,12,21,3,9,24,6,2,12,4,2,6]
##   i.e. a cascade state space of 5,778,664,237,486,728,806,400 tuples.
##   Constructing even a single cascade element exhausts memory at -o 14g.
##   This is a limitation of explicitly materialising the cascade, NOT
##   evidence against the decomposition: the skeleton, its depth 22, all 92
##   components and all 5 nontrivial groups reported above are exact, and
##   the holonomy theorem guarantees the cascade covers M.
################################################################################
